query: AlCrFeNiSi belongs to a high-entropy-alloy family developed to combine properties that traditional single-principal-element alloys often cannot achieve simultaneously. Earlier research sought stable solid solutions and adjusted HEA compositions to target particular properties, but tradeoffs persisted: the CoCrFeMnNi system has limited wear and corrosion resistance, manganese can promote oxidation and oxide spallation, and cobalt-containing systems raise cost and processability concerns. Conventional bulk fabrication can cause compositional segregation during cooling, whereas mainstream metallic additive-manufacturing techniques can generate residual thermal stresses that impair mechanical performance and increase processing complexity. Given cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock, what single intervention could improve mechanical integrity while limiting segregation, residual stress, and defect formation? State one hypothesis containing the intervention, its causal mechanism, a quantitative or directional outcome relative to conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi, the processing and test boundaries of validity, the prior evidence supporting it, and a decisive experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Consolidating gas-atomized cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi high-entropy-alloy powder by spark-plasma sintering (SPS) at 1000 °C under 50 MPa for 10 min will yield a fully dense, single-phase BCC/B2 microstructure with <2 at.% intra-grain elemental segregation, cut X-ray-measured residual stresses by ≥50 %, and raise room-temperature 0.2 % proof strength by ≈25 % relative to a vacuum-arc-cast AlCrFeNiSi baseline fabricated without SPS or post-HIP.
generation.material_initial_state: Gas-atomized AlCrFeNiSi powder (15–45 µm, spherical, <0.1 wt% O) stored under argon.
generation.intervention: Spark plasma sintering at 1000 °C, 50 MPa uniaxial pressure, 100 °C min⁻¹ heating rate, 10 min hold, vacuum <10 Pa, followed by furnace cooling in the SPS chamber.
generation.conditions: Specimen diameter ≤20 mm; no subsequent heat treatment; tests performed at 25 °C in air on as-SPSed versus arc-cast & homogenized (1100 °C/4 h/WQ) references.
generation.structural_mediator: Rapid Joule heating and axial pressure enable solid-state diffusion bonding of powder contacts, collapse gas pores, and suppress dendritic solidification, producing equiaxed ultrafine grains (1–2 µm) and a chemically-homogeneous BCC/B2 solid solution with nanoscale Ni–Al–rich precipitates.
generation.mechanism: 1) Fast thermal cycle limits long-range elemental partitioning, reducing microsegregation; 2) High pressure plus plasma cleaning removes surface oxides and closes internal porosity; 3) Uniform heating minimizes thermal gradients, lowering quench-induced residual stresses; 4) Fine grains and coherent precipitates strengthen by Hall-Petch and precipitation hardening, improving mechanical integrity without cobalt.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the arc-cast baseline: (i) density ≥99.5 % vs ~97 %; (ii) residual stress σ_res (XRD sin²ψ) ≤75 MPa vs ~150 MPa; (iii) segregation index (max – min composition over 10 µm EDS line) ≤2 at.% vs ~5 at.% ; (iv) 0.2 % proof strength ≈1120 MPa vs 900 MPa; (v) uniform elongation ≥10 % vs 8 %.
generation.baseline: Vacuum arc-cast AlCrFeNiSi ingot, homogenized 1100 °C/4 h, water-quenched: ~97 % density, ~150 MPa residual stress, ~5 at.% segregation, 0.2 % proof stress ~900 MPa, ~8 % elongation.
generation.boundary: Applicable for powder sizes 10–60 µm and SPS peak temperatures 950–1050 °C with holds ≤15 min. Below 900 °C insufficient densification occurs; above 1100 °C grain growth and phase separation may negate benefits.
generation.uncertainty: Exact strength increment and optimal temperature may shift with powder oxygen content and slight composition variations; long-term stability above 600 °C is unverified.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two specimen sets from the same powder lot: (A) arc-cast + homogenized (baseline) and (B) SPS per intervention. Measure: (1) density by Archimedes and micro-CT porosity, (2) residual stress by XRD sin²ψ, (3) compositional homogeneity by EPMA/EDS line scans, (4) phases by XRD, (5) grain size by EBSD, (6) room-temperature compression per ASTM E9 for 0.2 % proof stress and ductility.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If SPS samples show ≥2 vol % porosity, residual stress reduction <20 %, segregation >4 at.%, or proof-stress increase <10 % over baseline, the hypothesis is falsified.
